purpose: Machine-readable institutional architecture and signage grammar for the sequential OWS-001 through OWS-064 heavy rebuild. This registry supplements, but never weakens, the narrative canon or peak-quality doctrine.

VCF.identity: Clean biological optimism made ordinary: neighborhood food-culture service, cultivation, cold-chain, packaging and biotechnology should look hygienic, approachable and industrially ubiquitous rather than ominous by default.
palette_language: cool neutral refrigeration and service zones
localized yellow quality-hold overlays only when historically justified
massing_language: ordinary neighborhood service buildings for common sites
larger cultivation towers and biotech wings only where site function requires them
spatial_grammar: clean product and returned material separated
receiving before inspection and clean holding
public issue separated from sanitation and waste
cold-chain equipment tied to visible service plant
cultivation routes separated from packaging/dispatch where scale permits
VCF.failure_language: Failures begin at mundane biological/material interfaces—drains, gaskets, seals, filters, return streams, refrigeration and supposedly separated cultivation systems—before escalating into containment.
anti_patterns: fungus everywhere regardless of collapse phase
public and return flows sharing one undifferentiated room

Atlas.identity: Maintainable heavy industrial precision: machines, service access and workflow are visible, standardized and designed around rapid replacement, calibration and throughput.
palette_language: yellow lockout or hazard zones where justified
spatial_grammar: feed to process to inspection to rework to output
maintenance access parallel to production
parts issue near service routes
operators and freight use different paths when scale permits
Atlas.failure_language: Machinery remains understandable while service intervals shorten, repair stock disappears, failed lines are cannibalized and manual bypasses replace automation.
anti_patterns: random Create machines with no process chain
orange warehouse with no service architecture

PolyCore.identity: Materials-science escalation made spatial: controlled experiments, comparative test cells and increasingly desperate substitution programs should let the player read the sequence of failed material strategies.
palette_language: yellow isolation fields tied to specific failed trials
spatial_grammar: specimen intake to preparation to exposure/test to observation to failed-material quarantine to records
comparative cells should be sequentially readable
stronger later barriers should visibly build on earlier failures
PolyCore.failure_language: The architectural story is escalation from elastomers to composites, ceramic/mineral systems and deep barriers, with each solution buying time rather than immunity.
anti_patterns: test cells with no observation route
yellow quarantine used without a specific failure source

Pleroma.identity: Standardized movement at enormous scale: repeated freight geometry, route coding, docks, inspection and cold-chain infrastructure should make Pleroma recognizable across road, warehouse, retail-fulfillment and port contexts.
palette_language: red closure overlays only at late containment
spatial_grammar: inbound to manifest/inspection to sort to storage/cold hold to outbound
rejected cargo must interrupt normal flow visibly
vehicle and pedestrian paths separated where scale permits
backlog should accumulate at real choke points
Pleroma.failure_language: A system designed for constant movement becomes progressively clogged by inspection, quarantine, ration conversion, border control and final closure.

Aevum.identity: Premium regenerative medicine presented as calm, competent and desirable. The tragedy comes from treatment dependence and supply interruption, not from depicting the medicine as fraudulent from the start.
palette_language: emergency overlays introduced only as supply and capacity fail
massing_language: patient-facing entrance and calm clinical wings
research or preparation support behind public spaces
separate loading and clinical supply access
more prestigious massing for advanced facilities
spatial_grammar: reception to assessment to preparation to treatment to monitoring to recovery/follow-up
staff supply and waste routes behind patient route
cold-chain dependency physically connected to treatment areas
Aevum.failure_language: Successful medicine becomes dangerous to interrupt: rationing, overflow, missed treatment windows and biologic supply dependence appear before generalized ruin.
anti_patterns: pre-crisis facilities already portrayed as failed dystopian clinics

Helion.identity: Utility infrastructure built around safety zoning, redundancy and maintainable energy flow. Players should understand what power or coolant path failed and why the operators resorted to manual continuity measures.
palette_language: red shutdown/critical overlays where historically justified
spatial_grammar: generation/intake to conversion to distribution to control to isolation/maintenance
essential loads identifiable
operators can reach switching and pumps without crossing hazardous process zones
Helion.failure_language: Small insulation, seal and coolant problems cascade into manual switching, rolling outages, load shedding and emergency stabilization.
anti_patterns: power equipment with no flow path
generic hazard signs instead of feeder/load/pump identification

Blackglass.identity: Physically hardened information infrastructure whose surviving hardware can outlast the player's ability to interpret it. Security, routing, cooling, power and archive layers should be spatially explicit.
spatial_grammar: access control to network intake to routing/compute to archive to protected utilities to physical handoff
security layers should matter to exploration
cooling and backup power must support the data spaces they serve
Blackglass.failure_language: The facility may remain physically valuable while meaning is encrypted, fragmented or inaccessible; later Darknet return hooks must remain plausible.
anti_patterns: black room filled with server blocks
security doors with no access hierarchy
destroying the later-return reason by making every archive immediately readable

Asterion.identity: Clean aerospace engineering at scales ranging from tracking and mission support to component integration and launch-service infrastructure. Clearances, cleanliness and mission flow matter more than generic futurism.
palette_language: high-visibility service/hazard sectors where propellant or launch systems demand them
material_language: launch-service pipework and protected flight-hardware areas
massing_language: large doors and specialized cargo approach
spatial_grammar: component receiving to clean assembly to integration/test to mission control/tracking to launch/service logistics
flight hardware movement gets appropriate clearances
people, cargo and hazardous launch service use different routes where required
Asterion.failure_language: Interrupted launches, evacuation, off-world continuity and abandoned mission hardware preserve evidence outside ordinary terrestrial networks.
anti_patterns: assembly hall too small for its hardware
mission control inside hazardous service zone
launch plumbing with no service purpose

Emergency Authority.identity: Civil emergency infrastructure imposed onto existing civic, logistics or health architecture. Temporary barriers, inspection, decontamination and administrative control should visibly overwrite earlier normal-use buildings.
palette_language: institutional remnants of the building beneath
massing_language: controlled perimeter additions rather than unified corporate architecture
spatial_grammar: arrival to screening to inspection/decon to cleared/rejected routing
authority additions should visibly interrupt original circulation
Emergency Authority.failure_language: Temporary emergency controls grow denser and more contradictory as clean/dirty distinctions become harder to sustain.

Joint Research.identity: Cross-institution containment research assembled under emergency pressure, with equipment and architectural vocabularies from several corporate systems visibly sharing one site.
massing_language: existing research facility with obvious emergency additions
spatial_grammar: evidence/sample intake to comparative research to containment to incident review
institutional handoffs should be visible
Joint Research.failure_language: The site shows that separate corporate discoveries have finally been combined, but only after the crisis has outgrown ordinary institutional boundaries.
anti_patterns: mixed equipment placed without clear handoff logic

Meridian Military.identity: Field-command and firebreak infrastructure optimized for control, logistics, defensive action and increasingly desperate containment operations rather than corporate presentation.
spatial_grammar: command to communications to staging to perimeter/operation
military routes overlay existing civilian or industrial ones
firebreak geometry must reflect actual tactical/containment purpose
Meridian Military.failure_language: Civil protection hardens into territorial control and destructive firebreak doctrine as ordinary containment stops working.
anti_patterns: generic military base disconnected from the site it occupies

Continuity Science.identity: A scientific monitoring operation focused on collecting the scale-defining observation that breaks prior assumptions. It should look analytical, improvised and cross-disciplinary rather than corporately polished.
palette_language: hand-applied monitoring sectors and evidence labels
spatial_grammar: sensor/evidence intake to correlation to review to secure communication
physical displays should reinforce scale and direction of detection
Continuity Science.failure_language: The evidence becomes more certain and more geographically impossible at the same time.
anti_patterns: sensor equipment with no analysis space

Continuity.identity: A cross-disciplinary emergency synthesis organization that appropriates existing spaces and equipment. Continuity should look increasingly coherent intellectually while remaining architecturally heterogeneous and improvised.
massing_language: bunkers or hardened rooms only where inherited or urgently added
spatial_grammar: evidence intake to correlation to command decision to communications to secure archive/evacuation
multiple institutional evidence streams physically converge
Continuity.failure_language: The team finally understands how the pieces connect as the infrastructure and political capacity required to act are disappearing.
anti_patterns: evidence boards with no source material or workflow

Civilian.identity: Ordinary human spaces under pressure. These locations should preserve domestic and shelter routines, improvised adaptation and personal decision-making rather than acquiring a corporate visual language.
massing_language: retain believable residential or shelter architecture
emergency adaptation should sit on top of normal use
spatial_grammar: daily living remains legible
evacuation/refuge adaptations must connect to real entrances, service areas and information points
Civilian.failure_language: Institutional certainty gives way to individual choices: stay, flee, share, hoard, wait, search and improvise.
anti_patterns: empty domestic rooms with random rubble

Municipal.identity: Recognizable public infrastructure converted into emergency service: transit, water, refuge information and school relief should retain civic legibility beneath crisis adaptation.
massing_language: preserve the original civic building type
temporary emergency staging added where public circulation can support it
spatial_grammar: public arrival to information/service to exit
staff/service and utility routes remain plausible
closures block actual routes rather than decorative corridors
Municipal.failure_language: Public systems keep simplifying their mission—move people, keep water flowing, provide shelter, distribute food—as staffing and infrastructure collapse.
anti_patterns: municipal site with no original civic function
closures that do not affect actual circulation
